name: Carpet Extractor
definition: A commercial cleaning machine that applies water or cleaning solution to textile floor covering and recovers loosened soil and liquid through suction, using a self-contained head or a separate hose-and-tool arrangement.
includedScope: Commercial tank extractors used with approved carpet wands or powered tools
excludedScope: Hard-floor scrubbers and unattended flood-water recovery
headline: Carpet extractor systems, recovery metrics, drying risks and buyer verification
description: This technical profile separates documented spray-extraction functions and model specifications from WCB procurement assessment so buyers can compare carpet extractors within compatible operating and reporting boundaries.
metaDescription: Commercial carpet extractor guide covering spray extraction types, solution and recovery systems, representative models, drying factors and buyer checks.
disclaimer: This is an independent category reference, not model-specific purchasing, chemical, textile-care, hygiene or repair advice. Confirm carpet-maker instructions, current machine documentation, configuration, local compliance and service terms.

keyFacts.label: Cleaning cycle
keyFacts.value: Solution application, agitation or tool movement, then vacuum recovery
keyFacts.evidence: Official manuals and product pages describe applying cleaning solution and recovering dirty liquid through suction.
keyFacts.scope: Reviewed commercial extractors; agitation architecture differs by tool and model.

keyFacts.label: Machine formats
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed manufacturer ranges show self-contained machines and separate extraction tanks used with hoses and tools.
keyFacts.scope: Commercial spray-extraction equipment represented by the sources.

keyFacts.label: Tank arrangement
keyFacts.evidence: Official specifications state distinct solution and recovery capacities.
keyFacts.scope: Named models only; usable fill and shutoff boundaries may differ.

keyFacts.label: Drying outcome
keyFacts.value: Depends on recovery, passes, fibre, humidity, ventilation and applied solution
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer sources publish recovery-related features but do not establish one universal drying time across sites.
keyFacts.scope: WCB synthesis constrained to documented extraction functions; no category-wide drying claim.

systemFlow.name: Solution preparation
systemFlow.evidence: Manuals identify solution tanks and chemical-use instructions.
systemFlow.scope: Exact chemistry and dilution remain carpet- and manufacturer-specific.

systemFlow.name: Solution delivery
systemFlow.role: Meters and distributes solution to the cleaning head or tool.
systemFlow.evidence: Official documentation describes pumps, spray controls and jets.

systemFlow.name: Soil release
systemFlow.componentFamily: Brush, powered head or manual wand action
systemFlow.role: Combines solution and mechanical action at the textile surface.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturer sources identify brush systems or hand-tool movement for extraction cleaning.
systemFlow.scope: Agitation varies by model and accessory.

systemFlow.name: Vacuum pickup
systemFlow.role: Removes suspended soil and liquid from the carpet.
systemFlow.evidence: Official manuals describe suction and recovery paths.
systemFlow.scope: Recovery performance depends on setup and carpet condition.

systemFlow.name: Recovery storage
systemFlow.role: Contains dirty liquid for controlled emptying and cleaning.
systemFlow.evidence: Official specifications and manuals identify recovery tanks and emptying procedures.

variants.name: Compact self-contained
variants.taskScale: Spot areas, rooms and constrained routes
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator pushes or pulls a combined spray, brush and pickup head
variants.limitations: Smaller tanks can increase refill and drain frequency.
variants.evidence: Kärcher and Tennant position compact self-contained extractors for smaller areas.

variants.name: Large self-contained
variants.operatorRelationship: Walk-behind machine integrates solution, agitation and recovery
variants.limitations: Furniture density and transitions reduce achieved productivity.
variants.evidence: Nilfisk ES300 and Kärcher BRC 40/22 C are documented self-contained commercial extractors.

variants.name: Tank extractor with wand
variants.taskScale: Flexible rooms, stairs and upholstery with approved accessories
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator manages separate machine, hose and tool
variants.spaceConstraints: Hose routing and cable management are required
variants.limitations: Tool technique and hose length influence application and recovery.
variants.evidence: TASKI and Truvox sources show tank-format spray extractors and accessory use.
variants.scope: Only approved accessories and machine combinations.

variants.name: Continuous-operation or higher-capacity format
variants.operatorRelationship: Walk-behind or tank system with larger capacities
variants.limitations: Capacity does not remove the need for drying and textile checks.
variants.evidence: Official sources publish larger tank capacities for named models.
variants.scope: Named configurations; not a fixed category threshold.

performanceMetrics.name: Cleaning width
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Nominal active spray, brush or pickup width
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Head design and stated measurement basis vary
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not convert width directly into achieved area performance.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official model sources publish cleaning or brush widths.

performanceMetrics.name: Solution and recovery capacity
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Indicates nominal liquid carried and recovered between stops
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Nominal tank volume, not necessarily usable working volume
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Flow rate, soil load and shutoff level change the effective cycle.

performanceMetrics.name: Solution pressure and flow
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Units and measurement points differ across manufacturers
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Higher pressure is not a universal cleaning or textile-safety score.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Selected official specifications publish pump pressure or spray flow.
performanceMetrics.scope: Only when stated for the exact model.

performanceMetrics.name: Vacuum specification
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: One input to liquid recovery performance
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Power, airflow, vacuum and motor count are not interchangeable metrics
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Motor watts alone do not establish water pickup or drying time.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources publish different vacuum-system attributes.

performanceMetrics.name: Cable, hose and machine dimensions
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports route, outlet, transport and storage planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Accessory fit and operating envelope may exceed body dimensions
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Check the complete configured system, not only machine length.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official specifications publish dimensions, cord or hose data for reviewed models.

applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturer sources position extractors for hotels and commercial carpeted spaces.
applicationFit.scope: Compatible textile flooring and approved chemistry only.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Drying window, guest access, noise, elevators and storage should be tested together.
applicationFit.assessment: A compact machine can improve access but may increase refill cycles.
applicationFit.limitations: No source establishes suitability for every carpet, backing or stain.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Trial a representative room and corridor and measure return-to-service time.

applicationFit.evidence: Official sources identify commercial offices and public facilities as intended environments.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Furniture density and occupied-hour access can outweigh nominal width.
applicationFit.assessment: Route productivity should include setup, cable and furniture movement.
applicationFit.basis: Documented machine formats and application statements.
applicationFit.limitations: Published figures do not represent furnished-route output.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Time a complete representative zone including setup and cleanup.

applicationFit.evidence: Commercial extractor materials include schools, hospitals or institutional facilities among applications.
applicationFit.scope: General textile-floor cleaning; infection-control or disinfection efficacy is not established.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Chemical approval, drying control and cleanability need facility-specific governance.
applicationFit.assessment: Equipment selection cannot substitute for an approved hygiene process.
applicationFit.basis: Official application positioning and spray-extraction function.
applicationFit.limitations: No reviewed source proves disinfection outcomes.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Obtain facilities and infection-control approval for the full process and drying controls.

applicationFit.evidence: Tank extractors can be used with manufacturer-approved hand tools and accessories.
applicationFit.scope: Only accessories and surfaces listed for the exact machine.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Hose management, tool fit and recovery at vertical surfaces require separate evaluation.
applicationFit.assessment: Do not infer accessory compatibility from hose diameter alone.
applicationFit.basis: Official accessory-oriented product and manual information.
applicationFit.limitations: No universal tool interchangeability is supported.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Quote the complete machine-hose-tool set with part numbers and trial the intended surface.

componentStack.name: Solution tank, pump and jets
componentStack.evidence: Official manuals identify solution-system components and maintenance.

componentStack.name: Brush or agitation head
componentStack.role: Provides mechanical action to release soil.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturer sources describe model-specific brush systems.

componentStack.name: Vacuum shoe, hose and motor
componentStack.evidence: Official manuals document vacuum and recovery components.
componentStack.scope: Family labels do not establish cross-model compatibility.

componentStack.name: Recovery tank and shutoff
componentStack.role: Contains recovered liquid and protects the vacuum path from overfill.
componentStack.evidence: Official instructions identify recovery-tank operation and emptying.

componentStack.name: Power, cable and accessories
componentStack.role: Supplies electrical power and connects task-specific tools.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources publish regional electrical ratings and accessory configurations.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating vacuum motor watts as a drying guarantee
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources publish different vacuum attributes but no normalized universal drying time.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Measure applied liquid, recovered liquid and drying time on the intended carpet.
procurementDecisions.basis: Recovery depends on the complete system and environment.
procurementDecisions.limitations: WCB has not independently tested the models.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Run a controlled site trial with agreed moisture and return-to-service criteria.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Record jet, pump, brush, vacuum and operator-pass settings.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming hoses and tools interchange because connections look similar
procurementDecisions.evidence: Manuals and product pages define model-specific tools and operating instructions.
procurementDecisions.scope: Exact machine and approved accessory list.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Purchase and validate a complete supported system.
procurementDecisions.basis: Interfaces, flow, electrical load and recovery vary.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Require machine, hose, wand and hand-tool part numbers in the quotation.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm hose diameter, coupling, pump limits and tool electrical rating.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Equating equipment capability with carpet-maker approval
procurementDecisions.evidence: Machine manuals give chemistry boundaries but cannot establish every textile or adhesive compatibility.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Carpet, backing, dye and adhesive requirements precede machine selection.
procurementDecisions.basis: System suitability depends on materials outside the machine specification.
procurementDecisions.limitations: This profile does not verify textile colourfastness or adhesive condition.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain carpet-maker guidance and conduct a concealed-area test.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm maximum temperature, dilution and applied-flow settings.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Cable, noise, access and drying controls
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Selecting only by nominal cleaning width
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources publish machine dimensions and corded operating formats.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Operational controls and drying isolation can outweigh peak output.
procurementDecisions.basis: The cleaning process creates wet textile surfaces and uses cables or hoses.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Site occupancy and local safety rules vary.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Include barriers, outlet plan, cable route and ventilation in the method statement.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify supply voltage, circuit protection and cable inspection regime.

engineeringChecks.reason: Water, chemistry, heat and agitation can affect textile systems.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain manufacturer instructions and test an inconspicuous representative area.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Machine manuals require appropriate cleaning solution and operating practices.
engineeringChecks.scope: Machine evidence does not replace carpet-maker approval.

engineeringChecks.reason: Pumps, jets, hoses, lips and seals are model-specific.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Verify product number, serial range and current parts list.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official manuals provide model-specific service and operating details.

engineeringChecks.reason: Voltage, plug, cable and protection vary by region.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Confirm the quoted regional product number and site power provision.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official regional pages and manuals state market-specific electrical data.

engineeringChecks.reason: Residual moisture affects reopening time and can create operational risk.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Define and measure acceptance conditions during the site trial.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources document extraction and recovery features but not a universal site drying time.
engineeringChecks.scope: WCB procurement check based on the documented operating system.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-68:2021
standards.applicability: Particular safety requirements for spray extraction machines for commercial use.
standards.evidence: IEC identifies the standard's scope as commercial spray extraction machines for indoor use by trained or instructed operators.
standards.scope: Confirm regional adoption and applicability to the exact product.

developments.scope: International base standard; regional implementation must be verified.
